prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-17, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-17):
| Current ratio           | 1.22 |
| Retained earnings       | 20,151M |
| Current liabilities     | 15,620M |
| Current assets          | 19,045M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 16,227M |
| Total liabilities       | 56,835M |
| Total assets            | 73,090M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,575M |
| Revenue                 | 24,479M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows a modest profitability with EBIT of 2,575 on revenue of 24,479, but exhibits high leverage (total liabilities 56,835 on total assets 73,090) and a relatively thin current position (current ratio 1.22). Without detailed interest coverage data, the credit risk leans toward the lower end of investment-grade or near speculative-grade; given the leverage and coverage ambiguity, a BBB- assessment is conservative but not distressed.

DECISION: BBB-
